tickets.subject: [DevOps] Logging and monitoring basics
tickets.pointer:
**Logging and monitoring basics**

- Key: `SETUP-OBS`
- Builds: see the description below
- Pull via ADAM: `/ticket %ID%`
- Written at release `r3`

**What:** Logging and monitoring basics. In **ticvai-infra** (Terraform, in the `cell` module) and **ticvai-backend**: the OpenTelemetry SDK (already referenced by the starter) in each of the five deployables of ADR-0055 (commerce, access, operations, workers and ticvai-ai), exporting traces, metrics and logs over OTLP to an OpenTelemetry Collector in the cell, which writes them to the cell's Log Analytics workspace in Azure UAE North (audit R057; nothing leaves the region). Logs are structured, never concatenated, and carry the trace and correlation ids; they never hold guest names, emails, phone numbers, document numbers, card data or biometric templates, only the opaque subject id (docs/architecture/observability.md; ADR-0009: PII-free by construction, not by filtering). Metrics are Prometheus-compatible. One alert rule to start with (the 5xx rate of each host) goes to an Azure Monitor action group that emails the on-call person (DevOps until a rota exists). Dev and staging only; production is built before the first live tenant.

**Done when:** a request to a dev host can be followed from its log line to its trace by the correlation id; a deliberate 500 on a dev host raises an alert the on-call person receives within five minutes; and a search of a day's dev logs after the seeded test run finds no email address, phone number or card number.

The rest of the spec (contract, tables, screens) lives in ADAM at the release tag. OpenProject holds who, when, state and order.

**What:** Monthly partitions: create three months ahead, detach what retention has expired. Builds: `table access.scan_event`, `table kernel.inbox`, `table ledger.journal_line`, `table marketing.message_dispatch`, `table platform.audit_record`, `table platform.dead_letter`, `table platform.outbox`, `adr ADR-0044`, `adr ADR-0047`, `adr ADR-0056`. tickets.subject: [BE] Published read views for cross-module reads, generated from the lineage
tickets.summary: Published read views for cross-module reads, generated from the lineage
tickets.pointer:
**Published read views for cross-module reads, generated from the lineage**

- Key: `DB-READ-VIEWS`
- Builds: `adr ADR-0055`, `adr ADR-0016`
- Pull via ADAM: `/ticket %ID%`
- Written at release `r3`

**What:** Published read views for cross-module reads, generated from the lineage. Builds: `adr ADR-0055`, `adr ADR-0016`. A deriver reads handoff/api-data-lineage.json and generates, per owning module, the views other modules may read (894 cross-schema reads on 30 September; ADR-0055), applied by the migrations.

**Done when:** every cross-schema read in the Block A slice goes through a published view, the views regenerate with one command, and a raw cross-schema read is reported by the lineage check. Spec (4 October, CHG-FXP-005), ADR-0055 rule 2: another module reads a schema only through views its owner publishes (or the owner's in-process query interface), never raw tables; the owner is the schema's module in handoff/service-decomposition.json. Default for the shape: one view per (reader module, owned table) pair the lineage actually reads, in the owner's schema, named `<table>_for_<reader module>`, exposing only the columns the reader's operations read, with SELECT granted to the reader's deployable role (DB-ROLES). Reads routed `analytical` go to the reporting replica, never the primary (ADR-0016).

tickets.subject: [BE] One Postgres role per deployable; the AI role read-only
tickets.summary: One Postgres role per deployable; the AI role read-only
tickets.pointer:
**One Postgres role per deployable; the AI role read-only**

- Key: `DB-ROLES`
- Builds: `adr ADR-0055`, `adr ADR-0020`
- Pull via ADAM: `/ticket %ID%`
- Written at release `r3`

**What:** One Postgres role per deployable; the AI role read-only. Builds: `adr ADR-0055`, `adr ADR-0020`. In ticvai-backend, created by the baseline migration (MIG-BASELINE), one PostgreSQL login role per deployable of ADR-0055: commerce, access, operations, workers and ticvai_ai, each reading its password or token from the cell's Key Vault. Each role gets USAGE and SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE on the schemas its modules own (the schema owners in handoff/service-decomposition.json; workers runs every module's consumers, the outbox relay and the scheduled jobs, so it gets the schemas those touch), SELECT on the published read views of DB-READ-VIEWS, and nothing else: no CREATE, no ownership, no BYPASSRLS, so FORCE row-level security applies to every host. ticvai_ai writes only the ai schema (and ai.inbox; ADR-0058) and is read-only on the transactional schemas (ADR-0020). The tables are owned by a separate migration role that only SqlMigrationRunner uses.

**Done when:** each host connects with its own role from Key Vault; an INSERT from the ticvai_ai role into a transactional table, and from the commerce role into an operations schema (fnb), are each refused by PostgreSQL; no host role has BYPASSRLS or owns a table (a query on pg_roles and pg_tables in CI shows it); and a host role with no scope set on its session reads no rows from a table under FORCE row-level security. The schemas each role owns (handoff/service-decomposition.json under ADR-0055's five deployables, 4 October, CHG-FXP-005): commerce: identity, pii, platform, workforce, approvals, accreditation, tenancy, kernel, catalogue, pricing, promotions, seating, orders, payments, ledger, wallet; access: access; operations: inventory, fnb, retail, marketing, queue, maintenance, resources, venuemap, assets, games, rental, transport, subscription, whitelabel, reporting, sync (and control, in the control database, ADR-0039); ticvai_ai: ai (and ai.inbox), read-only on the rest; workers: the schemas its consumers, the outbox relay and the scheduled jobs write, which is every module's.

tickets.subject: [DevOps] Sign-in working end to end against IdentityService
tickets.summary: Sign-in working end to end against IdentityService
tickets.pointer:
**Sign-in working end to end against IdentityService**

- Key: `SETUP-AUTH`
- Builds: `operation identity#login`, `operation identity#refreshToken`, `operation identity#logout`, `operation identity#getCurrentSession`
- Pull via ADAM: `/ticket %ID%`
- Written at release `r3`

**What:** Sign-in working end to end against IdentityService. Builds: `operation login`, `operation refreshToken`, `operation logout`, `operation getCurrentSession`. The staff sign-in path of contracts/spine/identity.yaml: `login` issues the session and refresh token, `getCurrentSession` returns the Session with `effectivePermissions` and `permissionsByScope` (the effective permissions the done-when reads), `refreshToken` and `logout` end the loop; the operations themselves are built on their IdentityService tickets, this task wires them through the host. In **ticvai-backend** and **ticvai-frontend**: the identity sign-in operations, `ICurrentPrincipal` and `ITenantContext` filled from the session, signing keys from the cell's Azure Key Vault (audit R057).

**Done when:** a seeded staff member signs in from a web app and an app, gets their effective permissions, and a request without a session gets 401.

**What:** Per-tenant request budgets: a token bucket per tenant and audience, and a load-aware share per replica. Builds: `operation subscription#getPlan`, `adr ADR-0032`, `adr ADR-0064`. ADR-0064 (accepted 1 October), in the kernel middleware of the commerce, access and operations hosts: a token bucket per tenant and audience (guest/public, staff, service, partner) with counts shared through Azure Managed Redis, sustained rate and a 2x burst for 10 seconds from the tenant's plan (Plan.requestLimits) or the platform default; one tenant held to 25% of a replica's request slots only while the replica is above 70% of its limit; shedding guest and public first, staff and service last (ADR-0032); 429 with Retry-After and the RateLimit-* headers; if Redis is unavailable each replica falls back to its own in-process buckets (the limit divided by the replica count).

**Done when:** in a test with two tenants on one replica, the busy tenant gets the whole replica while the other is quiet, is held to 25% of the slots once the replica passes 70% while the quiet tenant's requests still succeed, a guest burst never spends a till's staff budget, and stopping Redis leaves requests served under the in-process limits. tickets.summary: AI gateway, governance decision point and usage metering
tickets.pointer:
**AI gateway, governance decision point and usage metering**

- Key: `AI-ENGINE-GATEWAY`
- Builds: `operation ai#setAiCredential`, `operation ai#setAiProvider`, `operation ai#evaluateAiGovernance`, `operation ai#getAiUsage`, `operation ai#testAiProvider`, `table ai.activity`, `table ai.decision_record`, `table ai.provider`, `adr ADR-0009`, `adr ADR-0020`
- Pull via ADAM: `/ticket %ID%`
- Written at release `r3`

**What:** AI gateway, governance decision point and usage metering. Builds: `operation ai#setAiCredential`, `operation ai#setAiProvider`, `operation ai#evaluateAiGovernance`, `operation ai#getAiUsage`, `operation ai#testAiProvider`, `table ai.activity`, `table ai.decision_record`, `table ai.provider`, `adr ADR-0009`, `adr ADR-0020`. setAiCredential, setAiProvider are served by ticvai-ai behind the AI gateway, to their contracts at the release tag in ADAM; no back-end task builds them. In ticvai-ai (Python). One gateway every AI call goes through: capability code calls gateway.run(task, inputs, schema?) and never names a provider (design 3.3). **Routing, in order:** (1) the allowed set: TICVAI's curated catalogue, filtered by the tenant's AI residency class (ADR-0009 amended 2 October, DEC-539): uaeOnly, the default and mandatory for government, bank and health tenants, resolves only to endpoints inside the UAE (Core42 Compass GPT-4.1 mini for the Small tier, Compass GPT-5 for the Strong tier, reached through the existing openaiCompatible provider kind); globalAllowed (a private venue under PDPL Art. 23) resolves to Azure gpt-5-mini / gpt-6-sol Global Standard or the tenant's BYOK provider; onPrem only when a client asks for it, and nothing is built for it in Block A (we host no LLM: Chinmay, 3 October, CHG-RONEP-004); then by the task's data classification and the governance policy; (2) the task's tier from TICVAI's curated task-to-tier map: a client never picks a model. BYOK accepts any vendor (CHG-FUP-008), is enabled by TICVAI (PLATFORM_AI_MANAGE) for a globalAllowed tenant only, maps each task to that vendor's equivalent model, and is activated by setAiProvider only after testAiProvider's compatibility probes pass (tool calling, structured output, Arabic, context, latency, residency); the key is a per-tenant write-only Key Vault secret shown only by its last four characters; (3) the cascade, Small to Strong only on a checkable signal (schema validation failed twice, retrieval partial), never on a model's self-reported confidence; (4) a circuit breaker per endpoint (opens at 50% errors over 20 calls or p95 above twice the task budget for 60 s; half-open after 30 s) and the class's fallback chain (uaeOnly: Core42 Compass, then OpenAI's UAE region; no LLM is hosted in the cell, so with both down the call goes to degraded mode); a residency refusal is returned, never failed over to another region; (5) degraded mode when nothing answers (search-only, rules-only or 'a person will help'). **Before each call:** the per-request budget and the capability's ceilingBehaviour, maskedFields (fail closed), then the scrubber and input guard of AI-ENGINE-SCRUB-GUARD, and a stable-first prompt order for prefix caching. **After it:** structured-output validation, the output guard and the re-fill, an ai.activity row and OpenTelemetry spans with no prompt text. evaluateAiGovernance is an in-process decision point (allow, allow with conditions, prepare only, approval required, escalate, block, with the policy version; design 3.8); getAiUsage meters tokens and spend per tenant; every governed answer writes one ai.decision_record (model, prompt template, policy and knowledge versions; design 3.9). About 12 engineer-days. **setAiProvider and setAiCredential are served here** (Chinmay, 3 October, CHG-RONEP-001): in Block A TICVAI staff enter a tenant's BYOK provider and key under the platform-staff grant on ADM-037 (no tenant self-service yet); the provider is checked against the curated catalogue and the tenant's residency class, and the key goes to the cell's Key Vault, never to a table in clear. About one engineer-day more (13). **Failover, in full** (DEC-539 as amended 3 October; CHG-R1S-001, CHG-R1S-002): a uaeOnly call goes to Core42 Compass by default and falls back only to OpenAI's UAE region (the ae.api.openai.com project); no LLM is hosted in the cell (we host none unless a client asks: Chinmay, 3 October), so with both down it answers in degraded mode. A residency refusal is returned, never failed over to another region, and failover never widens residency (CHG-R1S-016); global endpoints are called statelessly (no Assistants, Threads or Conversations, store=false, no uploads or fine-tuning).

**Done when:** a uaeOnly tenant's call reaches the Compass endpoint and, with Compass forced down, falls back to the OpenAI UAE endpoint, and with both forced down answers in degraded mode, never from a Global endpoint (a test asserts the residency refusal instead of a cross-border call); a BYOK provider that fails a compatibility probe is refused with 409 compatibility-test-required; a tenant over its ceiling gets the capability's ceilingBehaviour; and every call in the test run leaves an ai.activity row, and every governed answer a decision record naming its model, prompt and policy versions.

Rules first: read each guest-sellable product's category, subcategory, segment tags (level, audience), minimum height and age, duration, price band and language through the catalogue API with the venue's permissions; pick the one or two attributes that split the products most evenly, dropping any where one answer leaves nothing bookable (deterministic: the same catalogue gives the same questions); map each answer to a product, a category or a flow. Publishing is publishGuidedChoice by a person holding TENANT_PUBLISH; nothing is published automatically. A withdrawn mapped product, or new products no answer reaches, raise a new suggestion and never rewrite the published version. About 4 engineer-days.

tickets.pointer:
**Venue-map proposals: walkways from a raster plan and labels for extracted shapes**

- Key: `AI-ENGINE-VENUE-MAP-PROPOSALS`
- Builds: `table ai.proposed_action`, `adr ADR-0069`
- Pull via ADAM: `/ticket %ID%`
- Written at release `r3`

**What:** Venue-map proposals: walkways from a raster plan and labels for extracted shapes. Builds: `table ai.proposed_action`, `adr ADR-0069`. In ticvai-ai: the AI side of proposeWalkways and proposeVenueLabels for the venue-map import that ships in r1 (CHG-RONEC-001; BO-093 Map Import & Labelling, BO-094; ADR-0069; Chinmay, 4 October, CHG-AIPH-002). The operations' endpoints and their writes are the back-end tasks SVC-AI-AI-3 (proposeWalkways) and SVC-AI-AI-1 (proposeVenueLabels); this task is the model work behind them. Walkways: only for a raster plan (a scan, a photograph, an illustrated map, a scanned PDF read through the OCR step), where there is no geometry to subtract; where the import found hand-marked paths (VenueMapImportJob.handMarkedPaths) the proposal follows the marks, one segment per marked stretch between junctions with basis handMarked and a confidence for how cleanly the stroke was traced, a gap in a mark proposed as two segments and never bridged; otherwise basis auto or seen, with a confidence per segment, low-confidence segments shown and never filtered out. Labels: read the shapes venue-map.importVenueGeometry already extracted (never the drawing itself) and propose what each one is (kind and name), using scanned text near a shape as a hint (ocrHint says which text was used); text alone never creates a point or raises a proposal above what the shape supports. Both write ai.proposed_action through the gateway's decision point and stop: nothing is a path or a label until an operator accepts it, segment by segment (venue-map.acceptWalkwayProposals) and proposal by proposal (acceptVenueLabelProposals), on BO-093. The proposals are scrubbed and guarded like every call (AI-ENGINE-SCRUB-GUARD) and read only the tenant's own map and knowledge collection (ADR-0020; the label proposals read the venue's Qdrant collection, AI-ENGINE-QDRANT). An evaluation set of TICVAI's own drawings (raster plans with and without hand marks, CAD exports with labelled and unlabelled layers, Arabic and English text) joins the harness (AI-ENGINE-EVAL). With the provider down the import still completes: no proposals are raised and BO-093 says the AI proposals are unavailable, never an empty network presented as complete. About 2.5 engineer-days.

**Done when:** a raster plan with hand-marked paths gets one proposed segment per marked stretch with basis handMarked and its confidence, and a gap stays a gap; a raster plan without marks gets segments with a confidence each, the low ones shown; extracted shapes get kind and name proposals that cite their ocrHint where they used scanned text; nothing is applied until an operator accepts it, segment by segment and proposal by proposal, on BO-093; it answers through the AI gateway with the scrubber and the guard on, its evaluation set passes the gate of docs/architecture/ai-system-design.md 3.5, it degrades as 3.7 says when its provider is down, and a peer AI engineer has reviewed it.

- Key: `AI-ENGINE-SCRUB-GUARD`
- Builds: `adr ADR-0020`, `adr ADR-0009`
- Pull via ADAM: `/ticket %ID%`
- Written at release `r3`

**What:** PII scrubber in our worker and the provider's safety service in front of every LLM call. Builds: `adr ADR-0020`, `adr ADR-0009`. In ticvai-ai, for every residency class (ADR-0020 amended 2 October, DEC-542/543; contracts/satellite/ai.yaml AiPolicy.scrubbing, CHG-CSA-003). We host no LLM (Chinmay, 3 October, CHG-RONEP-004): the scrubber runs on the AI GPU node pool in our own cell, Presidio's recognisers on its CPU and the Arabic named-entity model on its GPU beside the embedding model (Chinmay, 4 October, CHG-R11-001), and the guard is the provider-side safety service. Between the gateway's maskedFields step and the provider: (1) detection with Microsoft Presidio (offline) and custom recognisers for Emirates ID numbers, UAE phone numbers, passport numbers, IBANs, Luhn-checked card numbers and email addresses, plus an Arabic named-entity model (CAMeL Tools or an Arabic GLiNER) for Arabic names and places; (2) reversible placeholders ([GUEST_1], [PHONE_1]) whose map lives in the cell for the life of the request only, is never logged and never travels with the prompt, and the reply re-filled before the user sees it; (3) the provider-side safety service (Azure AI Content Safety in UAE North by default, not a guard model of ours) on the prompt before it leaves and on the answer before it is shown, a streamed answer checked as it arrives; a guard model of our own only if a client asks for one; (4) mandatory whatever the residency class: a uaeOnly tenant is scrubbed as well; (5) fails closed: scrubber (or its GPU node) or safety service down means 503 scrubber-unavailable and no provider call; a guard refusal is 422 guard-refused. maskedFields stays the first control; the scrubber is the second, for free text. About 6 engineer-days.

**Done when:** on a test corpus in Arabic and English, a prompt carrying an Emirates ID, a UAE phone number, an IBAN, a card number, an email and an Arabic name reaches the provider stub with placeholders only and no raw value, and the reply comes back re-filled; stopping the scrubber or the safety service refuses the call with 503 and the provider stub receives nothing; a harmful prompt is refused with 422 guard-refused; and the corpus test runs in CI on every gateway change. In ticvai-ai, the scrubber on the AI GPU node pool in our own cell (CHG-R11-001) for every residency class (ADR-0020 amended 2 and 3 October, DEC-542/543, CHG-R1S-002; (3) a second, deterministic pattern pass after Presidio (Emirates ID 784-..., +971 numbers, Luhn card PAN, IBAN, email): any survivor blocks the call (CHG-R1S-016); Presidio's version pinned and recorded on every call (it is community-maintained now: take a release on purpose, after the corpus passes); each call writes its scrub audit (entity counts by type, never values; AiInteraction.scrubAudit); a value planted to slip past Presidio is caught by the pattern pass and blocks the call;

**What:** The planner agent on top of the rules planner. Builds: `operation venue-map#updateVisitPlan`, `table venuemap.visit_plan`. In ticvai-ai: the planner agent on top of the rules planner in venue-map (design 2.3 and 7; MOB-6). The schedule is solved deterministically (OR-Tools CP-SAT over show times, opening hours, walking times and configured capacity; research T04) and the Small tier reads the guest's intent and writes the why. The agent works only through the plan operations as the guest (the itinerary kind of requestSuggestion and its plan tools), never writes venuemap.visit_plan itself, and is grounded in each day's venue: it proposes only what that day's tools return, and a wish the venue cannot meet is answered from VisitPlan.unmatchedPreferences. When AI is off or fails it falls back to the rules plan, never to an error. About 8 engineer-days.

**Done when:** a refinement in chat (add lunch at one, skip the coasters) produces a valid plan through the plan tools that respects show times and capacity; a request for something at another venue is answered from unmatchedPreferences and updateVisitPlan refuses the point (422 point-not-at-day-venue); and with the model stubbed down the guest gets the rules plan.

**What:** The on-sale waiting room: Redis positions, the cached page, the release controller, admission tokens. Builds: `operation catalogue#enterWaitingRoom`, `operation catalogue#getWaitingRoomPosition`, `operation catalogue#setWaitingRoomSetting`, `adr ADR-0064`, `adr ADR-0066`. ADR-0066 (accepted 1 October; B1, or Block A if an on-sale is booked in Block A): enterWaitingRoom gives a position from a Redis counter with no database write; the static branded waiting page is served from Front Door's cache and polls getWaitingRoomPosition; a release controller admits guests per second from the health of commerce (latency and the 429 rate, ADR-0064); an admitted guest gets a short-lived signed token (tenant, performance, expiry, unique id; key in Key Vault) that middleware checks by signature, with no database read, on addCartLine and acquireInventoryHold from guest channels only (till, kiosk and workstation holds are exempt, amendment of 1 October); activation follows the performance's onSaleFrom/onSaleTo or setWaitingRoomSetting.

**Done when:** with the room on, a guest cart hold without a token is refused 403 admission-required, one with a valid token succeeds, a forged or expired token or one for another performance is refused, a till hold needs no token, and the release rate drops when commerce latency rises.

tickets.subject: [FE] Kiosk shell: the published kiosk configuration on KSK-001, KSK-002, KSK-008, KSK-010, KSK-013 and KSK-014: build with all states
tickets.summary: Kiosk shell: the published kiosk configuration on KSK-001, KSK-002, KSK-008, KSK-010, KSK-013 and KSK-014: build with all states
tickets.pointer:
**Kiosk shell: the published kiosk configuration on KSK-001, KSK-002, KSK-008, KSK-010, KSK-013 and KSK-014: build with all states**

- Key: `APP-KIOSK-CONFIG#build`
- Builds: see the description below
- Pull via ADAM: `/ticket %ID%`
- Written at release `r3`

**What:** Builds: `operation white-label#getPublishedKioskConfig`. The kiosk shell reads its group's published kiosk configuration (getPublishedKioskConfig, keyed by the kiosk's workstation) at start and at every return to the attract loop, caches it with the loop's media for offline, and applies it: KSK-001 plays the attract loop (the group's slides, transition, sound, play windows, the closed loop outside the opening hours, the Download our app QR slide) under Touch to start, and runs the idle rule on every kiosk screen (Still there? with its countdown, then the cart cleared, the guest signed out, back to the loop in the default language); KSK-002 offers the group's languages with its default; KSK-008, KSK-010 and KSK-013 show the group's payment unresolved, printer failure and call staff messages; KSK-014 shows the group's out of service message and expected-back time. Offline the last cached loop plays and nothing is sold. Scope: getPublishedKioskConfig on KSK-001, KSK-002, KSK-008, KSK-010, KSK-013, KSK-014; the rest of each screen is its own ticket (APP-KIOSK-KSK-001, APP-KIOSK-KSK-002, APP-KIOSK-KSK-008, APP-KIOSK-KSK-010, APP-KIOSK-KSK-013, APP-KIOSK-KSK-014). Decided by Chinmay, 5 October 2026 (AM-WHITE-LABEL-KIOSK, CHG-R4-003). Done when KSK-001, KSK-002, KSK-008, KSK-010, KSK-013, KSK-014 call getPublishedKioskConfig as their specs say (every state the wired components list, the cached answer offline where the spec says so, every refusal the contract documents), the rest of each screen still passes its own ticket's done-when, and a peer in the same stack has reviewed it.

The rest of the spec (contract, tables, screens) lives in ADAM at the release tag. OpenProject holds who, when, state and order.
